N/A

A 48-year-old woman with an 8-month history of painful bilateral thoracic and lumbar paravertebral muscles spasms. These spasms lasted from 10 to 30 seconds and were accompanied by severe pain that gradually disappeared over another 30 seconds. Contractions occurred spontaneously but were also elicited by anxiety and startle reactions. Symptoms occurred throughout the day and occasionally during sleep. In-between periods of exacerbation, she felt fluctuating discomfort and rigidity in the cervical, thoracic and lumbar axial muscles, including scapular girdle, leading to an almost persistent upright posture.

Gait was slow with noticeable axial stiffness.

Electromyography with nerve conduction studies revealed continuous activity of the lumbar paraspinal muscles. Cerebral spinal fluid analysis was normal with no oligoclonal bands. Cranial and spinal cord MRI were unremarkable. Screening for breast, lung, and ovarian malignancy was negative.

extractions.quote: Past medical history was positive for depression, refractory to a 3-month trial of amytriptyline 75 mg qd and to current treatment with venlafaxine 150 mg qd. Routine laboratory exams included normal leucocytes count, with mild Coombs-positive anemia (Hb 10.3 g/dL) and thrombocitopenia (120,000/ml); erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 79 mm/h. During this interval, she developed photosensitive rash on the forehead and upper extremities, metacarpo-phalangeal arthritis, fatigue, and brief episodes of confusion that interfered with job performance as a nurse.
